workflows.name: Text to Video
notes: Supply a non-empty `prompt`. Use concrete motion and camera instructions, for example a tracking shot, a slow pan, or a stationary camera. Select the output framing with `aspect_ratio`.
To animate existing images, use `kling-video/v4.0/image-to-video`. To guide a new video with image or video references, use `kling-video/v4.0/reference-to-video`.

Use the exact field names and values listed above. `duration` must be an integer from 3 to 30, and `resolution` must be `720p` or `1080p`. Omit unused media fields instead of sending empty strings or nulls.
The schema permits additional properties, but undocumented keys do not create new model controls. Use only the parameters documented for this endpoint.
A non-empty prompt is required. Use one of the four listed aspect ratios; `adaptive` is not allowed for Text to Video.

price.note:

HDR adds $0.047 per second of output video at 1080p or $0.078 at 4K, after base-price discounts, including fixed-price agreements. SDR has no additional charge.

workflows.name: Image to Video

help.fr: Images intermédiaires, dans l’ordre : Kling les place lui-même entre le début et la fin (8 au plus).
help.en: In-between frames, in order: Kling places them itself between the start and the end (8 at most).

notes: Frames are sent in this order: `image_url` → each entry in `image_urls` → `end_image_url`, if supplied. Put middle frames in the order you want them used. The schema allows at most 8 middle frames, leaving room for one first frame and one end frame: up to 10 images in total.
Only `image_url` is required. An end frame or middle frames alone cannot start a valid request. Omit unused optional frame fields rather than sending empty URL strings.
This endpoint does not expose an `aspect_ratio` parameter. Prepare your input frames with the desired composition; use `resolution` to select 720p or 1080p output.

Use the exact field names and values listed above. `duration` must be an integer from 3 to 30, and `resolution` must be `720p` or `1080p`. Omit unused media fields instead of sending empty strings or nulls.
The schema permits additional properties, but undocumented keys do not create new model controls. Use only the parameters documented for this endpoint.
The first frame is required even when middle or end frames are supplied. Nine or more middle frames are rejected. `aspect_ratio` is not a documented control for this mode.

notes: A prompt alone is insufficient. Supply at least one non-empty `image_urls` or `video_urls` list. Empty lists do not satisfy the reference requirement.
Images are addressed as `@image_1`, `@image_2`, and so on, and videos as `@video_1`, `@video_2`, and so on, following array order.
This mode creates a new video from references. To edit an existing source video, use `kling-video/v4.0/video-edit` and its required `video_url`.

Each supplied video URL is subject to a 2 GiB download limit. Input videos longer than 30 seconds are trimmed to their first 30 seconds before generation. This does not change the requested output `duration`, which remains an integer from 3 to 30 seconds.

Use the exact field names and values listed above. `duration` must be an integer from 3 to 30, and `resolution` must be `720p` or `1080p`. Omit unused media fields instead of sending empty strings or nulls.
The schema permits additional properties, but undocumented keys do not create new model controls. Use only the parameters documented for this endpoint.
A prompt with no usable reference is invalid. An empty reference array does not satisfy the source requirement.

notes: `video_url` is the required source video to edit. `video_urls` contains optional reference videos; it does not replace the source. `image_urls` contains optional reference images. A source video plus a prompt is sufficient; references are not required.
The source is `@video_1`. Reference videos from `video_urls` start at `@video_2`, in array order. Reference images start at `@image_1`, in array order.
`duration` controls the requested output duration; it is not automatically copied from the source video's length.

Each supplied video URL is subject to a 2 GiB download limit. Input videos longer than 30 seconds are trimmed to their first 30 seconds before generation. This does not change the requested output `duration`, which remains an integer from 3 to 30 seconds.

Use the exact field names and values listed above. `duration` must be an integer from 3 to 30, and `resolution` must be `720p` or `1080p`. Omit unused media fields instead of sending empty strings or nulls.
The schema permits additional properties, but undocumented keys do not create new model controls. Use only the parameters documented for this endpoint.
A reference video in `video_urls` does not satisfy the required `video_url`. Keep the source and reference roles separate.

workflows.name: Reference to Video
notes: Provide a non-empty `prompt` of at most 7,000 characters. `duration` is an integer from 4 to 15 seconds, including every whole-second value in that range; it defaults to 5. `resolution` accepts `480P` or `768P` and defaults to `768P`.

Provide at least one non-empty reference list: `image_urls` (up to 9), `video_urls` (up to 3), or `audio_urls` (up to 3). These references guide the generation; they are not first or last keyframes. Use the Image to Video variant for keyframe control.

Reference media is prepared before generation. Video clips may be resized, transcoded, trimmed or extended; the prepared video references have a combined duration of at most 14.8 seconds. Input-video charges use that prepared duration, which can differ from the original files.

Use the `aspect_ratio` values listed in the parameter table. Where offered, `auto` and `adaptive` derive framing from the input; text-only requests fall back to `16:9`. `aigc_watermark` is fixed to `false`.
Use URLs accessible to the service. The documentation examples use placeholder media URLs; replace them with your own image or media URL before sending a request.

price.note: 480P: $0.04 per second of output video and prepared input video. 768P: $0.06 per second of output video and prepared input video. Total = (output seconds + prepared input-video seconds) × the selected per-second rate + additional-image charges. Input-video duration is measured after preprocessing, which may trim or extend the clips.

workflows.name: Reference to Video

Reference media is prepared before generation. Video clips may be resized, transcoded, trimmed or extended; the prepared video references have a combined duration of at most 14.8 seconds. Input-video charges use that prepared duration, which can differ from the original files.
